behavior: C0 registers command/address/data. C1 decodes the request and launches the existing two-cycle RAM.
C2 produces register_second or registered RAM data; output enable opens at C2 and closes at C3 unless another read follows.
No extra data output register is added after the two-cycle sources. The MCU sees the current halfword before its subsequent capture edge.
Byte address and all command/status register definitions remain unchanged. READ never implicitly ACKs or releases a block.
ACTIVE stores row state; PRECHARGE closes it. Only MRS bank0/address0230 enables normal register and RAM accesses.
constraints: Keep port names, high-active reset, row decoder and ADC/DDR block ownership contracts unchanged.
Use J20 SRCC, native BUFG clock, CAS3, RPIPE2 and RBURST disabled. Keep existing 2-cycle XPM RAM read latency.
Constrain DQ to a rising-edge virtual capture clock with 2 ns MCU setup plus 0.5 ns provisional board budget, and 0.25 ns uncertainty.
Keep 16 independent IOB tristate FFs. The new data output is a KEEP fabric net for ILA; never route IOB FF Q back into fabric.
corner_cases: Illegal row/mode or unavailable owned RAM returns DEAD and latches error.
CKE low cancels an outstanding read and disables output. A stopped clock during reset must still release DQ.
Consecutive halfword reads must return their own current word; output must release before a legal host write.
Auto-precharge and explicit PRECHARGE close row ownership without shifting register addresses.
verification_cases: Old C3-launch implementation fails the C3-minus-2ns read-data check; repaired implementation passes.
Register ID/version/status/scratch, byte writes, SET200/START order and explicit ACK/RELEASE.
4096-word full RAM block, 40-byte tail, invalid window access and short low/high SDCLK duty cases.
Read-to-write handover and asynchronous DQ release during active read.
Independent interface implementation and complete original-project copy with matching ILA probes; hardware acceptance remains to be performed.
